report.source_text: Direct laryngoscopy revealed a submucosal cystic lesion immediately beneath the mobile vocal cords without any significant patent airway around the cyst (figure 2A). Using a 22-gauge microlaryngeal needle, 1 mL of thick yellowish clear fluid was aspirated from the cyst. The cyst arising from the right posterolateral wall of subglottis was marsupialised using coblator.

report.source_text: Postoperatively, child recovered well and was discharged with a corked tracheostomy tube and nasal breathing. Follow-up endoscopic evaluation at 2 months did not suggest cyst recurrence. Delayed decannulation following exclusion of recurrence has been planned to ensure avoidance of any emergent visit to hospital during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and nation-wide lockdown.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-month-old girl with a history of prematurity and prolonged intubation presented with noisy breathing, progressive biphasic stridor, and respiratory distress. Physical exam showed tachypnoea and biphasic stridor worsened on crying with suprasternal and intercostal retractions. Direct laryngoscopy identified a submucosal cystic lesion immediately beneath the vocal cords causing airway obstruction. COVID-19 test was negative. The child underwent tracheotomy and cyst marsupialization. Postoperatively, she recovered well, with no cyst recurrence at 2-month follow-up and planned delayed decannulation.
